fast.note: Was 46/48, then 48.5/49.3 until the M1 tuning pass refitted it (3,000 seeds, kept to the hundredth so a quarter of races read slow). Set near the 25th and 75th percentile of the leader's half on the shipped card, so about a quarter of races read hot and a quarter slow. The sim's clock starts at the gate with no run-up and its horses slow less through a race than real ones, so its halves run one to two seconds slower than real charts.

cruiseFeetPerSecond.note: Set so the shipped card's median winning time at 10 furlongs on fast dirt is about 2:01.5.

kickBoostShare.note: Steep on purpose so +10 kick is worth about as much as +10 speed or stamina; a kick-70 horse still gets 6.5 percent. Below kick 41 the line goes negative and the sim treats it as no extra gear.

askFeetToGo.note: Stalkers and closers ask at about the 5/16 pole, so an M1.4 move at the 3/8 pole is a real change. Front-runners kick on a little earlier, which kept the three styles within the fairness tolerance.

earlyEffort.note: Front-runner was 1 (M1 tuning pass). It sets only two things: the duel peak (this plus frontRunnerPace.duelEffort) and a rated front-runner's effort (this less rateEarlyEffortDrop). Lowered with duelEffort raised, so the peak stays at 1.035 and a rated front-runner runs at 0.97, below a lone leader's 0.98: rating hands over the lead instead of being a free saving.

frontRunnerPace.note: Short presses and a costly duel, so a hot half usually means front-runners fought and paid for it. The duel still peaks at 1.035 of cruise (earlyEffort.frontRunner plus duelEffort; duelEffort was 0.035 with earlyEffort.frontRunner at 1), because every pressed leader of any style is pushed toward the same peak and a cheaper peak steepened the post slope for stalkers and closers. pressLengths was 1.5 (M1 tuning pass): shorter presses end duels sooner, and at 1.5 three front-runners won 10.7 percent each against a fair 12.5.

formSpeedShare.note: Kept small: when form moved speed a lot, a hot half mostly meant a front-runner having a good day.

laneWidthFeet.note: Narrower than a horse on purpose: at 2 feet, 8 identical horses showed the inside posts winning about 2.5 points too often.

rateEarlyEffortDrop.note: Was 0.01 (M1 tuning pass). With earlyEffort.frontRunner at 0.9825 a rated front-runner runs at 0.97, a stalker at 0.9775 and a closer at 0.9675.

rateEarlyUntilShare.note: Was 0.5 (M1 tuning pass). Shorter rating narrows the gap between a card with two front-runners and one with three.

earlyMoveGearShare.note: Was 0.05 (M1 tuning pass). At 0.05 the first 330 feet of a 3/8 move burned about 0.15 of the reserve, and the move lost for 15 of 16 horses measured.

saveForStretchKickShare.note: Was 0.03 (M1 tuning pass). Raised so a stalker saving it still gains more after the quarter pole than one given no instruction (I4) once presses got shorter (the duel peak did not change).

stayInsidePassMarginShare.note: Added in the M1 tuning pass. A horse told to stay inside goes around a horse in front only when that horse is this much slower than it wants to go (everyone else uses traffic.passMarginShare). When it never went around, it lost 2 to 6 points of win share for every horse measured, for about half a length of ground saved.

laneSpeedShare.note: Was 0.005 (M1 tuning pass), raised with laneWidthLanes narrowed so the bias pays the rail itself.

laneWidthLanes.note: Was 2 (M1 tuning pass). Horses run at lane 0.4 to 1.2 through the turns on their own, so at 2 lanes most of the field already had most of the bias and holding the rail gained nothing from it.

blockedPerHorse.note: The chance a horse is unlucky this way today. It becomes an event only if the race puts it in the situation within windowFeet, so about 2.6 percent of horses are blocked per race on the shipped card (M1.5, 2,000 seeds).

steadiedPerHorse.note: As blockedPerHorse: about 1.1 percent of horses are steadied per race on the shipped card.

bumpedPerHorse.note: As blockedPerHorse: about 1.1 percent of horses start a bump per race on the shipped card. Bumps fire more readily than blocks, since horses are often side by side.

windowFeet.note: About two seconds of running. Longer windows let a passing glimpse of traffic count as much as being stuck behind a horse, and stay inside stopped making a horse blocked more often.

aheadLengths.note: The model holds a horse to the speed of one within blockLengths in front, so this is a horse that is right on its heels.

steadiedSpeedDropShare.note: Cost rises steeply with this share: in M1.5 tuning runs 0.08 cost a steadied horse about 0.4 lengths at the wire on average, 0.11 about 1.4 and 0.15 about 2.3.

bumpedSpeedDropShare.note: Was 0.08 (M1 tuning pass), lowered when bumpedReserveShare was added so a bump costs about what it did. Bumps find horses with neighbours on both sides more often than the rail horse, so a costlier bump steepened the post slope for stalkers.

bumpedReserveShare.note: Added in the M1 tuning pass. Both horses in a bump lose this share of their reserve. With a speed cost alone, a front-runner bumped early dropped out of the speed duel and finished no worse, sometimes better.
